chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Jameel ibn Salih, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I stand in the prayer and see the faeces in front of me towards the Qiblah.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Move away from it as much as you can, and do not pray upon the centre of the road.'
ai.seo_question: What should one do if faeces are seen in front of them during prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of removing minor impurities (al-‘adhrā) from the prayer space, emphasizing that while complete removal is ideal, moving away as much as possible suffices if the obstacle cannot be fully cleared. It also introduces the concept of 'al-jawadd' (the center of the road), which Shia jurists interpret as a place of public transit and potential soiling, thereby rendering it a disliked place for prayer due to the likelihood of impurity or disrespect. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on both physical purity (taharah) and spiritual reverence (khushu') in the location of salah.
